newsitem.title: spain: Cuba's blackballing of envoy a mistake - Madrid.
newsitem.headline: Cuba's blackballing of envoy a mistake - Madrid.

text.p: Spain's conservative government warned Cuba on Tuesday it had made "a big mistake" by reportedly withdrawing the Spanish ambassador's credentials in protest at Madrid's new hard line against Cuban leader Fidel Castro.
"It's a big mistake, in a word," Foreign Minister Abel Matutes told state radio. "It looks more like an unjustified tantrum than a serious, responsible reflection on the blockade Cuba is under."

Matutes said Madrid had yet to receive formal notice of the Cuban move against its ambassador -- "withdrawing the placet" in diplomatic terms -- which according to local media was announced in Tuesday's issue of the official newspaper Granma.
The "placet" -- Latin for "it pleases" -- is the formal acceptance by the host country of another state's envoy. It is usually granted when an ambassador is officially nominated.
The Cuban embassy in Madrid told Reuters a statement would be published in Granma but declined to confirm the details.

Havana's reported move caps weeks of growing tension with Madrid, where conservative Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar has broken with the friendly approach towards Castro favoured by his predecessor Felipe Gonzalez during 13 years of Socialist rule.

At Aznar's behest, Spain is now trying to push its 14 European Union partners into a harder line against Castro that would mesh in with Washington's efforts to push for democracy in Cuba, including a ban on trade.
Castro blasted Aznar without naming him in a speech on Sunday, accusing him of taking money from what he described as a mafia of Cuban exiles in Miami.
